cadcraft-cli: headless CADCraft

Usage: cadcraft-cli <COMMAND>

Commands:
  info       Print a drawing's summary as JSON
  convert    Convert a drawing; OUT's extension picks the format (dxf, dwg, dwt, svg, png, pdf)
  run        Open drawings (or start a new one), run scripts and commands in order, save or export the result
  commands   Print the command catalog as JSON
  mcp        Run the MCP server on stdio: a headless drawing session, or a bridge to the running app
  perf       Time the engine on a synthetic N-entity drawing (default 200000), or the canvas display-list build of a drawing, zoomed in step by step
  sample     Write a built-in sample drawing
  roundtrip  Open each DXF/DWG, save it as DXF and DWG, reopen and compare; writes report.md and report.json
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Craft Anything on the command line: every tool, the MCP server, setup and doctor.

Usage: craft-anything-cli.exe [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  mcp           Run the MCP server on stdin/stdout
  setup         Connect Craft Anything to your coding-agent apps
  doctor        Check the install, registrations, engines, AI backends and the MCP server
  uninstall     Remove Craft Anything's registrations and skill from agent apps
  commands      List every tool
  capabilities  What this install can do: toolsets, tool availability, engines
  triage        Open a file and run a first look at it
  report        Write a readable investigation report (Markdown or HTML) from findings and evidence
  chat          Ask the AI agent a question about a target (streams to stdout)
  rebuild       Study a website, app or game and have a coding agent rebuild it in a new project folder
  ai            Manage AI backends
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>    Output format. `--output-format` always means this, even after a tool that has its own `--format` [default: json] [possible values: json, jsonl, md, text, csv, tsv]
      --js

deckcraft-cli works on DeckCraft presentations (.deckcraft, .pptx) without a window.

  info               print a presentation's slides, layouts and theme as JSON
  render             draw slides as PNG images
  render-transition  draw frames of the transition into a slide as PNG images
  convert            save a presentation in the format OUT's extension names
  run                run commands on a presentation, then save or export it
  commands           list the commands run can use, one per line
  describe           explain one command and its parameters
  app                run a command in the DeckCraft app started with --control
  mcp                serve the commands to an agent over MCP on stdio
  bench              time opening, drawing, saving and exporting a presentation
  links              print the DeckCraft community and project links
  --version          print the version

A presentation is edited by running commands on it:

  deckcraft-cli run --cmd 'slide.new={"title":"Q3 results"}' --save q3.deckcraft

`deckcraft-cli help SUBCOMMAND`, or `deckcraft-cli SUBCOMMAND --help`, explains one subcommand;
`deckcraft-cli help run` explains how to write a command.

lightcraft-cli — headless LightCraft (photo library + raw developer)

USAGE:
  lightcraft-cli run [OPTIONS] COMMAND [key=value | '{json}']… [COMMAND …]…
      Run one or more commands (ids from `commands`, or control-protocol methods such as
      engine.commands / ui.inspect / ui.screenshot) and print one JSON line per command:
      {"command", "ok", "result" | "error", "ms"}. A word without `=` starts the next
      command; values are JSON when they parse (1, true, [1,2], {…}), else strings. Exit status
      is non-zero when a command fails. Example:
        lightcraft-cli run --import ~/Photos/a.jpg develop.set control=light.exposure value=0.7 \
            develop.auto app.export path=/tmp/a.jpg longEdge=1600
      Options:
        --demo            headless, the procedural demo library
        --library DIR     headless, open (or create) a LightCraft library; edits are saved
        --import PATH     headless, import a file or folder first (repeatable)
        --connect [ADDR]  drive the running app (`lightcraft --control 7980`; default 127.0.0.1:7980)
        --script FILE|-   also run JSON lines {"command": id, "params": {…}} (or {"method": …})
        --keep-going      c

vectorcraft-cli — VectorCraft automation

USAGE:
  vectorcraft-cli mcp [--connect ADDR | --headless] [--automation-read-root DIR]... [--automation-write-root DIR]...
      Run the MCP server on stdio. Default: connect to a running app at 127.0.0.1:7979
      (vectorcraft --control 7979), falling back to a headless in-process session.
      --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root confine the files the agent's commands read
      (open, place, relink, library loads…) and write (save, export, package, library saves…) to
      DIR, links followed; each may be given more than once, a path inside any of its folders being
      allowed, and a kind left out grants none of its access. They imply --headless: a running app
      enforces its own (vectorcraft --control PORT --automation-read-root DIR …).

  vectorcraft-cli run [--in FILE] [--cmd ID [--params JSON] | --commands FILE|-]... [--export FILE]... [--scale N] [--ppi N]
      Headless batch: open FILE (any readable format) or start a new document, run commands in
      order, export each FILE in the format its extension picks (see Writable formats; a .ait FILE
      is a template, written as file.saveAsTemplate writes it). Ras
